title: NY State Senate · District 15
area: Central and southern Queens, including Ozone Park, Woodhaven, Howard Beach, Richmond Hill and the Rockaways.

context.text: Incumbent Joseph Addabbo defeated Albert Baldeo in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 77.8% to 21.6% (7,427 to 2,064 votes). He faces Danniel Maio, the Conservative Party nominee, in the general election.

candidates.name: Joseph Addabbo
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary against Albert Baldeo, 77.8% to 21.6%

summary.text: Joseph Addabbo Jr. is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Senate District 15, representing central and southern Queens since 2009. A lifelong Queens resident and the son of a former U.S. Representative, he practiced law for about a decade and served seven years on the New York City Council before his 2008 election to the Senate, where he chairs the Committee on Racing, Gaming and Wagering. He is seeking re-election against Conservative Party candidate Danniel Maio.

background.text: Born in 1964, the youngest child of Joseph and Grace Addabbo; his father, Joseph P. Addabbo Sr., was a former U.S. Representative. He describes himself as a lifelong Queens resident.
Attended Nativity BVM School in Ozone Park and Archbishop Molloy High School, then earned a bachelor's degree from St. John's University (1986) and a law degree from Touro Law School (1992).
Practiced law for about ten years, including as an attorney at Addabbo and Greenberg, before entering the City Council.
Served as Executive Secretary of Community Board 10Q and as president of the Ozone Tudor Civic Association, both former roles listed in his official biography.
Elected to the New York City Council in 2001 and served seven years representing the 32nd District, working on infrastructure, school technology and community-services funding.
Elected to the New York State Senate in 2008 and assumed office in 2009; won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for re-election over Albert Baldeo.

Chairs the Senate Committees on Racing, Gaming and Wagering and on State-Native American Relations, and is a member of the Budget and Revenue, Cities 1, Education, Insurance, Rules, and Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs committees.

According to his official biography, he is a multi-term member of the New York State Democratic Committee, ranking member of the South Queens Regular Democratic Club, a member of Ozone Park Kiwanis and of the Senate Bipartisan Task Force on Hurricane Sandy, and a 2026 New York State Senate Veterans' Hall of Fame Honoree. He is married to Dawn and they have two daughters.

priorities.text: Describes his role as legislative advocacy for "children, the elderly, families, working people, consumers and veterans," alongside environmental protection, economic development and government accountability.
priorities.quote: children, the elderly, families, working people, consumers and veterans

positions.summary: Has repeatedly opposed the Manhattan Central Business District Tolling Program, introducing legislation to delay its enforcement and arguing it burdens taxi and truck drivers, seniors, people with disabilities, and outer-borough businesses.
positions.quote: While the contradictory program aims to reduce traffic congestion and simultaneously bolster funding for our public transit system from vehicles paying the toll, it also poses significant financial challenges to various groups, including local businesses, taxi drivers, truck operators, the elderly, and individuals with disabilities.

positions.summary: Voted yes on the GREAT Act (S9500-A), which creates a statewide virtual power plant program aimed at reducing reliance on fossil-fuel peaker plants and supporting the state's clean-energy targets.

record.text: Chairs the Senate Committee on Racing, Gaming and Wagering and the Committee on State-Native American Relations; also serves on the Budget and Revenue, Cities 1, Education, Insurance, Rules, and Veterans, Homeland Security and Military Affairs committees.
Sponsored S10104, which would expand the list of bail-eligible offenses to include offenses involving physical harm or danger to others; remained in the Senate Codes Committee as of April 29, 2026.

Sponsored S10059-A ("Brendon's Law"), which would create new penalties for motor vehicle speed contests, sideshows and street takeovers and authorize vehicle seizure; amended and recommitted to the Senate Transportation Committee on April 28, 2026.

Sponsored S10069, which would enhance know-your-customer and responsible-gaming requirements for mobile sports wagering; remained in the Senate Racing, Gaming and Wagering Committee as of April 27, 2026.

summary.text: Danniel Maio is the Conservative Party candidate for NY State Senate District 15. A retired candidate with a 1984 bachelor's degree from American University, he has appeared on general-election ballots for Congress (2016), State Assembly (2018, 2020), State Senate (2022, 2024) and City Council (2023), losing each, and has no record of holding office. He is on the Conservative Party line after not appearing on the 2026 Republican primary ballot.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from American University in 1984; is retired.
Was the Republican candidate for U.S. House in New York's 6th District in 2016, losing the general election to incumbent Grace Meng.
Ran for State Assembly District 28 in 2018 as the Republican nominee and in 2020 on the COVID19 Stories Party line, losing both general elections to incumbent Andrew Hevesi (13.4% in 2020).
Ballotpedia lists him among withdrawn or disqualified candidates for the 2019 special election for NYC Public Advocate (Nonpartisan) and the 2021 Queens Borough President race (Republican).
Lost the 2022 State Senate District 15 general election to incumbent Joseph Addabbo, receiving 42.6% (22,643 votes) on the Republican, Conservative, Medical Freedom and Independence lines.

Lost the 2023 New York City Council District 29 general election to incumbent Lynn Schulman as the Republican and Conservative candidate, and the 2024 State Senate District 15 general election to Addabbo on the Conservative line.

Is on the November 2026 ballot on the Conservative Party line and, per Ballotpedia, on the No Kings Party, Queens United Party and 4 Our Immigrants Party lines; he did not appear on the Republican primary ballot.

priorities.text: In a 2022 Ballotpedia candidate survey for this same seat, listed crime, schools, and taxes and inflation as his three key campaign messages.
Says he is focused on the needs of seniors and children.

Describes his approach to office as auditing how government spends money: reviewing how officials vote and spend, whether programs actually reach and satisfy the people they are meant to help, and publicizing out-of-order city services and equipment.

positions.summary: Listed stopping congestion pricing in Manhattan among the policy positions he is passionate about.

He has no record of holding office. No official or campaign biography of Danniel Maio beyond his Ballotpedia profile was found, so his biography is limited to education, profession and his candidacy history.
